summary: Nvidia releases Cosmos world models for interactive simulation and agentic AI training

sentences: Physical AI developers working with world models face two distinct challenges: adapting models to their sensors, tasks, and data, and getting those models into applications reliably.
Cosmos is a platform of world foundation models and development tools for physical AI .
Cosmos Framework provides agent skills and recipes for world model training, multimodal data processing, optimization and inference.
Cosmos NIM microservices supports GPU-accelerated serving through application APIs.

The simulation section shows how to use Cosmos Framework’s inference recipes and agent skills to generate synchronized camera video and LiDAR observations for AV, robot, and surgical scenarios, starting from released checkpoints you can run today.
The deployment section shows how to choose a NIM configuration for your GPU, launch the container, verify readiness, and send your first inference request.
Cosmos Framework is an open and fully modular framework for world model training, model optimization, and inference to support a full model development lifecycle using new agent skills.
It is expanding beyond Cosmos 3 to support NVIDIA Alpamayo , GR00T, Qwen, pi0.5, and other compatible Hugging Face models.
Load the setup, inference, post-training, and troubleshooting skills under .agents/skills .

Cosmos Framework provides post-training and inference recipes for robot simulation, realistic scene generation, multi-camera driving simulation, and surgical policy evaluation.

New Cosmos 3 Nano simulation recipes and example checkpoints enable developers to use agent runnable skills to evaluate our example checkpoints and adapt Cosmos 3 Nano to custom sensors, action space, and data domains.
These checkpoints support PyTorch and vLLM-Omni, tested on NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs.
Use the recipe to select GPU count, memory configuration, and inference settings.
Both AV checkpoints take a prompt and World Scenario Map (WSM) controls representing lanes, objects, road markings, traffic signs, and road boundaries.
Joint RGB–LiDAR generation additionally uses HD-map rangemap controls and supports optional initial LiDAR observations.
Prompts describe weather, lighting, time of day, road conditions with prefixes providing camera-rig and field-of-view context.
An optional initial camera images provide visual context to guide the generated scene’s appearance.
Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto uses bidirectional generation to denoise an entire multi-view clip at once for offline synthetic data generation .
It supports 30 fps input and output video, with up to 400 frames at 480p or 720p; longer sequences can be generated through autoregressive chunking.
Change the prompt to turn a daytime drive into a rainy night while keeping the same road layout and vehicle trajectories.
Use these variations to train and evaluate perception and driving models across weather and lighting conditions.

For Transfer-Auto, use the published sample configuration with seven synchronized WSM videos, per-camera captions, first-frame RGB conditioning, and HD-map LiDAR controls.
See the Transfer-Auto inference guide for setup, input preparation, and output details.
The reference run produces seven 720p videos (297 frames at 30 FPS) and 99 LiDAR sweeps.
Check sample_outputs.json for success and lidar.safetensors for finite range and intensity values, then verify WSM alignment and consistency across camera views and LiDAR.
For custom scenarios and rig adaptation, see the WSM renderer and Transfer-Auto post-training guides .

Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto is the causal, few-step-distilled variant of Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto, enabling autoregressive streaming generation.
It generates observations incrementally as an AV policy or human driving input updates the scenario through a WSM renderer.

Generated camera and LiDAR observations return to the policy, enabling closed-loop evaluation
For Sim-Auto, reproduce the reference rollout using the published Sim-Auto sample checkpoint and pre-rendered WSM controls to generate synchronized camera videos and LiDAR observations autoregressively.
See the Sim-Auto inference guide for setup, input configuration, and output details.
For human-controlled rollouts, see Sim-Auto Interactive Drive .
The Sim-Auto reference run writes to outputs/sim_auto/daytime_scene/ .
Apply the same output checks described above for Transfer-Auto.
Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Transfer converts depth video and a prompt into RGB video with varied lighting, textures, and backgrounds while preserving geometry and motion.
For robot demonstrations, it changes the third-person view while retaining actions, states, and wrist-camera recordings.

Turn depth, segmentation, edges, or blurred video into detailed RGB observations, using language prompts while the simulator maintains physical state
Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual generates the next visual observation from the scene and robot actions.
It supports interactive two-arm simulation for YAM and AgiBot embodiments, controlled by a policy or human-operated joysticks.
Here, Sim-Transfer generates visuals from a physics simulator’s updated state; Sim-Bimanual generates the next observation directly from the scene and robot actions.
Surgical environments are among the most challenging for classical simulators due to their complex multi-physics nature.

Generative simulation offers a complementary approach: rather than explicitly modeling scene geometry, tissue deformation, and physical interactions, world foundation models learn visual dynamics directly from synchronized surgical video and robot kinematics.
Cosmos3-H-Embodied-Nano , built on Cosmos3 and post-trained on Open-H-Embodiment, generates surgical video from robot actions, predicts actions from video, or generates both together.
It takes an initial RGB frame, a task prompt, the last 16 executed actions, and subsequent robot actions.
Developers can use it to generate synthetic data and evaluate policies offline without building a physics model of the surgical scene.
Cosmos3-H-Dreams lets developers test how a surgical policy responds as a procedure unfolds, with each action shaping what happens next.
Distilled from Cosmos3-H-Embodied-Nano, this causal, few-step model generates frames from live robot kinematics for real-time, closed-loop simulation controlled by a human or learned policy.
This gives developers an interactive environment to explore surgical maneuvers and evaluate policies before testing on physical hardware.
